description: Putting part of a course on a digital tool is expected to help only through the method it makes affordable (more practice with feedback, adaptive hints, prompts to explain, visible progress) and not through the medium itself; no claim here tests a digital against a non-digital version of the same method.
title: Digital Learning

description: For a learner with no working method for a structured target, explicit explanation, modelling and guided practice with checks is expected to beat minimally guided discovery on near-term performance, qualified by task-specific expertise, age, outcome type and horizon.
title: Direct Instruction

description: For adolescents who read adequately in general but meet a discipline's texts as novices, a semester or more of instruction that names, models and has them practise the discipline's own reading and reasoning moves on its own texts is expected to improve comprehension of new texts in that discipline and the practised kind of disciplinary thinking; two studies test this against usual or textbook instruction, none against generic strategy instruction, and the one writing measure showed no gain.
title: Disciplinary Literacy

description: For learners studying a topic in which race shapes outcomes or experience, naming race explicitly around a shared text, case or data set, under agreed norms with optional disclosure and a closing debrief, is expected to yield more specific, better-evidenced analysis than neutral treatment or unstructured talk without raising risk for learners in the minority; no claim in the wiki tests this.
title: Discussing Race

description: For a task too large for one learner to hold or do alone, putting part of the work into shared representations, tools or partners is expected to raise performance with those aids present, and to build what the learner can do alone only when the parts the target requires stay with the learner and the learner's decisions to rely on aids are calibrated; no claim recorded in the wiki tests distributed against individual work at first hand, while single studies test how much to hand to an AI tool, feedback that calibrates offloading, and the form of a group's shared representation.
title: Distributed Cognition
